newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish ex-minister says rallying anti-Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turkish ex-minister says rallying anti-Islamists.

text.p: A minister who resigned from the Turkish coalition government at the weekend said on Monday he had made progress in talks with the opposition on forming a new government that would exclude the ruling Islamists.
"I am very hopeful about the contacts I have made. We will get an alternative to this government," Yalim Erez, the former trade and industry minister, told Reuters.

Some secularist politicians have called for the formation of a broad-based alliance to squeeze Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan out of office and then form a secularist coalition without going to elections.
Parliamentary sources said conservative Erez had met leading members of the main opposition Motherland Party and a secularist left-wing grouping.
Previous attempts at secularist unity in parliament have failed due mainly to rivalry between Erez's True Path Party and Motherland.
Erez and another minister resigned on Saturday in a row over Erbakan's failure to implement anti-Islamist measures demanded by the army.
